summary: Module utilities are shared helper code; every Python module must import from ansible.module_utils (commonly AnsibleModule). The namespace is built dynamically per task, modules may only import from ansible.module_utils.*, and local module_utils directories merge into it.
questions: Can my module import from ansible.errors or other parts of the ansible package?
How do I share code between several of my custom modules?
What must every Python Ansible module import?
Why does my module fail on the target when importing from ansible.parsing?

answer_card.title: Module utilities basics
answer_card.answer_md:
- All Python modules must import from `ansible.module_utils`, typically `from ansible.module_utils.basic import AnsibleModule`.
- `ansible.module_utils` is built dynamically per task from the configured search path.
- **Only** import from `ansible.module_utils.*`; other `ansible` imports (e.g. `ansible.errors`) are unsupported because the package may not exist on the target.
- Share code by putting it in `./module_utils/my_shared_code.py` and importing `from ansible.module_utils.my_shared_code import MySharedCodeClient`; local dirs merge into the namespace in search-path order.
